newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 28.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on October 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl of Germany and President Suharto will hold bilateral talks at the Freedom Palace in central Jakarta. The talks will focus on economic and trade issues.
Garuda Indonesia, the country's national carrier, yesterday launched its first cargo jet

The head of the Indonesian police, Lieutenant General Dibyo Widodo, said that the death of a man charged with robbery while in police custody would be investigated. Widodo said investigators would examine who was responsible for the death of the man, who had allegedly been tortured while in police custody.
Separatist gunmen killed an Indonesian soldier in the troubled territory of East Timor on Thursday last week, the military commander in the area said.

Bambang Suharto, head of Kosgoro, a unit of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party, said that he has had no talks so far with Guruh Sukarnoputra. It has been rumoured that Guruh, brother of ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader, Megawati Sukarnoputri, and a member of the PDI himself, is considering changing his political allegiance.
Germany's Chancellor Kohl spent a leisurely day fishing in the Thousand Islands off Jakarta before the start of bilateral talks today.

The Indonesian economy was likely to grow by 7.5 percent in 1997 against an expected 7.3 percent in 1996 despite political uncertainties and a slow-down in export growth, an Indonesian economic think-tank said.
